# envoy-rust STATE.md — Historical Reference Archive

> This file holds historical narrative blocks relocated verbatim out of
> `STATE.md` per **ADR-0035** (see `docs/envoy-rust/DECISIONS.md`). It exists
> solely to keep `STATE.md` small enough to read in full at cold-start while
> preserving every prior-commit narrative byte-for-byte per doctrine D-3.4
> (context isolation) + D-3.5 (decisions/narratives are written, not deleted).
>
> **This file is read-on-demand, NOT required at cold-start.** The cold-start
> procedure (`BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §1 Step B) requires reading `STATE.md` in
> full; this archive is consulted only when a session needs the historical
> detail behind a `STATE.md` pointer.
>
> Content is append-only and preserved verbatim: every "THIS commit" reference
> inside a relocated block retains its original meaning (it resolves to the
> commit named in that block's own "Historical reference (preserved …)" header
> or subsection) and must not be rewritten. Original section/subsection
> headings and ordering are preserved. The `## Relocated from …` headings below
> are organizational wrappers added at relocation time to identify each
> block's origin in `STATE.md`.

---

- **gRPC family** — gRPC bridge, gRPC-Web, gRPC-JSON transcoding, interop conformance.
- **xDS / dynamic config family** — ADS, delta xDS, LDS, CDS, RDS, EDS, SDS, RTDS, reconnection, initial-fetch timeout.
- **Observability family** — gRPC ALS, OTLP access log, OTel/Zipkin/Jaeger/Datadog/XRay tracing, stats sinks, tap filter.
- **Runtime + hot restart family.**
- **WASM host family** — own multi-phase sub-project; ABI, engine binding, proxy-wasm conformance.

Originates at phase-02.2's ADR-0015 landing (where `host.docker.internal` was introduced as the BACKEND_HOST substitution for cross-container reachability via `host-gateway`); subsequent phases 02.2 / 03.1 / 03.2 / 04.1 / 04.2 did not push to CI between phase-02.1 close (run `24913934580`) and 04.3 task 14 (run `25106213773`), so the regression has been latent across **five phases**. Envoy v1.33's tightened `socket_address.address` parse semantics expect either a literal IP (under `STATIC`) or DNS resolution opt-in (under `STRICT_DNS` / `LOGICAL_DNS`):

```
[critical][main] [source/server/server.cc:416] error initializing config '/etc/envoy/envoy.yaml':
malformed IP address: host.docker.internal. Consider setting resolver_name or setting cluster type
to 'STRICT_DNS' or 'LOGICAL_DNS'
```

The 04.3 REVIEW reviewer's verdict choice was **(b) "Approved with M-track follow-ups" — defer to a dedicated post-04.3 fixture-hardening sub-phase** (or roll into phase 05 brainstorm scope), on the rationale of cross-phase scope spanning 5 fixtures and 4 phases, schema growth not in 04.3's planned deliverable set, original-budget-fit concerns, and the fact that fixture 0008 inherits the broken pattern uniformly with the four pre-04.3 fixtures. The recommended forward work:

1. Add `ClusterType::StrictDns` to the envoy-config schema at `crates/envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs::ClusterType` (currently single-variant `Static` enum at lines 60-62); this also closes the dormant phase-02.1 REVIEW I3 (positive `ClusterType::Static` variant-name regression guard) in the same scope by giving the second variant.
2. Validator accept path for `STRICT_DNS` cluster type.
3. Coordinated-edit of the 5 affected fixtures (`tests/fixtures/{0003,0004,0005,0006,0008}/envoy.yaml` + per-fixture `envoy-rust.yaml` mirror) to use `type: STRICT_DNS` where `host.docker.internal` is the backend host literal.
4. Re-push to CI to confirm green Docker-gated runs across all 5 fixtures including 0008.

The phase-05 brainstorm session is the natural place to choose between (a) folding C-1 into phase 05's scope as a Task-1 preamble, (b) splitting C-1 into a separate fixture-hardening sub-phase (e.g. `04.4-fixture-hardening` or `05.0-fixture-hardening`) that lands before phase-05 HTTP/2 work begins, or (c) ratifying the deferral and continuing against the unit-test gate. Doctrinally option (b) is the cleanest shape per the M-track follow-up posture.

Items carrying forward to phase 05.3 (recommended closure-targets):

- **I1 (Important; CI h2spec tarball lacks integrity verification).** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:43-49` provisions h2spec via `curl -fsSL ... | sudo tar xz -C /usr/local/bin` with no SHA-256, no GPG, no tag-pinning beyond version string. Blast radius is contained (CI runner ephemeral; envoy-rust source checked out before install) but a release-pipeline takeover or DNS hijack could inject arbitrary code. **Fix sketch**: capture published SHA-256 from the GitHub release page, hardcode, verify after download. **Disposition: carry forward to 05.3 (or as a standalone 05.x security-pass).**
- **I2 (Important; `Http2Error` variant overload at the response-emission edge).** `crates/envoy-http2/src/response.rs:60-69` openly admits two misnomers: `send_response()` failures map to `H2StreamAccept` (line 77; "accept" implies inbound), `send_data()` failures map to `H2BodyRead` (line 81; "read" implies inbound). The variant names imply inbound/accept paths but are used for outbound/send paths. Source `h2::Error` retains diagnostic fidelity, but the typed wrapper is misleading on stack traces and log lines. **Fix sketch**: add `H2ResponseSend { source: h2::Error }` + `H2BodyWrite { source: h2::Error }` variants (or rename `H2StreamAccept` → `H2StreamIo` if a single duplex variant is preferred). Public API change but no external consumers yet — additive variants are cheap. **Disposition: carry forward to 05.3, BEFORE the upstream H2 client introduces additional H2 error sites that would amplify the misnaming.**
- **I3 (Important; `MalformedH2HeaderBlock` is a coarse catch-all hiding three distinct failure modes).** `crates/envoy-http2/src/error.rs:40-50` documents the variant as covering structural pseudo-header issues, non-token byte names, and non-UTF-8 byte values; in practice it's also raised for `HeaderName::from_bytes` failure on the response side, `HeaderValue::from_str` failure, and `HttpResponse::builder().body(())` failure (`crates/envoy-http2/src/response.rs:49-57`). When a request-side translation failure hits this variant, an operator looking at logs cannot tell whether it was a non-UTF-8 header-value byte (request-side, defensible 400), an unrepresentable response status, or a stale state-machine bug elsewhere. **Fix sketch**: split into `InvalidHeaderName { name: String }`, `InvalidHeaderValue { name: String }`, `InvalidResponseHead`. Public API impact bounded since callers currently only `match` exhaustively in tests. **Disposition: carry forward to 05.3.**
- **M2 (per-stream `tokio::spawn` task carries no per-test or per-fixture timeout).** `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:78-82` spawns each H2 stream task without a wall-clock budget. Latent in 05.2 because the only `BuildOutcome::Proxy` arm is the 502-stub which returns synchronously. **Fix sketch**: add a per-stream `tokio::time::timeout` budget when 05.3 wires the upstream H2 dispatch (the budget fits naturally there since the upstream call is the long-tail). **Disposition: carry forward to 05.3 or 08.**
- **M8 (502 Bad Gateway stub body literal mentions phase 05.3).** `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:132` emits body `b"upstream H2 not yet wired (sub-phase 05.3)\n"`. SPEC §6 local signpost 21 explicitly accepts "doctrine-line is sufficient." When 05.3 replaces the stub, this literal disappears. **Disposition: trivial 05.3 entry-point check; closes at 05.3.**
- **M10 (`differential::Driver::Http2` variant lacks `extra_headers`).** `tests/differential/src/lib.rs:86-96` carries `method/path/host/expected_status/expected_body/expected_headers` but no `extra_headers: Vec<(String, String)>` field (compare `Http1Probe` at lines 175-191). 05.2's only fixture (0009) does not need it; 05.3 may. The `drive_http2` helper already accepts an `extra_headers` parameter (`tests/differential/src/lib.rs:806`); only the enum variant lacks the field. **Fix sketch**: at 05.3 when fixture 0010 lands, add the field with `#[serde(default)]` and thread it through the dispatch arm. **Disposition: carry forward to 05.3.**
- **M11 (`Http2Error::MissingAuthority` recovery path is RFC-soft).** `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:78-82` (the spawn site) logs the per-stream error via `tracing::error!` and lets the task end without sending any response. RFC 9113 §8.3.1 requires a request without `:authority` (and without a `Host:` header) to either be rejected by the codec layer or generate a 400 from the server. envoy-rust currently produces no response. **Fix sketch**: raise a 400 Bad Request from the stream task on `MissingAuthority` (and other request-translation failures) instead of dropping silently. Maps to envoy-rust's H1 `synth_400` posture. **Disposition: carry forward to 05.3 or 06+.**

Items carrying forward to phase 06+ (recommended closure-targets):

- **I1 (Important; ADR-0028's option-(B) deferral leaves an H1-listener × H2-cluster silent runtime protocol-misnegotiation).** ADR-0028 deliberately defers the H1-listener H2-arm dispatch (the H1 listener cannot dispatch to a cluster whose `upstream_protocol = Http2` because adding `envoy-http2` as a dep on `envoy-http1` would cycle). The deferral is correct doctrine — but the deferred path is not gated at parse time, so a configuration with `codec_type: AUTO` (or `HTTP1`) on the listener and a cluster with `typed_extension_protocol_options.HttpProtocolOptions.http2_protocol_options` set does NOT fail validation; it silently runs H1-on-the-wire to an H2-only upstream backend, which would either get rejected by the backend or produce a confusing 502. **Fix sketch**: add `ConfigError::Http2ClusterFromHttp1Listener { listener: String, cluster: String }` parse-time gate at the envoy-config validator (cross-validate listener `codec_type` against each cluster's `upstream_protocol` per route), or add a runtime defense at the H1 router-arm `BuildOutcome::Proxy` site that catches the misconfiguration with an explicit log + 502. **Disposition: carry forward to phase 06+.** Phase 06's brainstorm should consider folding I1 as a Task-1 preamble (the parse-time gate is a small validator extension).
- **I2 (Important; typed-error chain dissolved at the dispatch site).** `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs`'s symmetric H1-or-H2 router-arm dispatch (Task 7, `52b3635`) collapses `Http2Error` variants to a 502 string at the wire via `to_string()`-shaping. The reviewer's specific finding: when the upstream H2 client returns `Http2Error::UpstreamConnect` (TCP refused) vs `H2ClientHandshake` (h2 handshake failed) vs `H2RecvBody` (body drain mid-stream), the on-the-wire response is identical (`502 Bad Gateway` with body `upstream connect error`-ish text); operators looking at logs see the typed variant in `tracing::error!`, but the response gives no signal. **Fix sketch**: structured `x-envoy-upstream-rq-failure-reason` response header reflecting the typed variant (envoy parity), or per-variant body text. Public API change but additive. **Disposition: carry forward to phase 06+.**
- **05.2 REVIEW I1+I2+I3** (CI tarball SHA-256 / Http2Error write-path variant rename / MalformedH2HeaderBlock overload split): **NOT CLOSED in 05.3.** Per 05.3 PROGRESS preamble paragraph 3, the SPEC §3 D1 explicitly preserved the 05.2 codec-side variants unchanged ("the 05.2 codec-side variants ... stay unchanged"). All three carryforwards continue to phase 06+.
- **05.2 REVIEW M11** (RFC-soft `MissingAuthority` recovery path): **NOT CLOSED in 05.3.** The per-stream task error handling at `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs` was unedited at the upstream-direction work; M11 continues to carry forward awareness-only.

Awareness-only Minor findings (per REVIEW §3 M1-M8):

- **M1** — `crates/envoy-http2/src/client.rs::ClientStream::send_request`'s comment-vs-code drift: the doc-comment claims "synthesizes :method/:path/:authority/:scheme: http"; the implementation also synthesizes `:scheme: https` if the connection is TLS-bearing (which 05.3 doesn't yet exercise but the code branches on it). Awareness only — defensive future-proofing. **Track until phase 06+ TLS+H2 work surfaces this.**
- **M2** — `Client::connect`'s `tokio::spawn` to drive the h2 connection has no `JoinHandle` retention; the spawned task is fire-and-forget. If the connection task panics (h2 internal bug), the panic is logged via tracing but not surfaced to the caller. Standard tokio pattern; awareness only.

Items carrying forward to 06.2 / 06.3 (recommended closure-targets):

- **I1 (Important; admin handler lacks idle read timeout — slow-loris-style resource hold).** `crates/envoy-admin/src/handler.rs:44-67` `read_request` loops on `stream.read(...).await` until either `MAX_REQUEST_HEAD = 8 KiB` is exceeded, `find_crlf_crlf` succeeds, or the peer closes (n == 0). A connected-but-silent client holds the connection open indefinitely, blocked on the kernel's read; the connection task in `JoinSet` stays parked. Compare the data-plane HCM at `crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:24` which sets `IDLE_READ_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5)` and wraps each per-request read in `tokio::time::timeout(IDLE_READ_TIMEOUT, ...)`. The shutdown path's `DRAIN_BUDGET = 5s` bounds the worst-case shutdown delay, but the steady-state hold is unbounded. **Fix sketch**: wrap the `stream.read(...)` call in `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), ...)` and map the `Elapsed` to a 408 Request Timeout (or just close — both proxies' admin scrape clients should retry on close). Mechanical, scoped to one site, ~10 LoC. **Disposition: carry forward to 06.2 or 06.3.** Whichever sub-phase first touches the admin handler is the natural close site. The 06.2 SPEC has admin-side access logging OUT OF SCOPE per cross-sub-phase rule 6, so 06.2 likely does not touch the admin handler by default — but the 06.2 PLAN-writer may opportunistically close I1 with a small no-scope-creep PR if the LoC budget allows. The 06.3 SPEC's comprehensive stats-wiring scope may touch the admin handler indirectly; if so, I1 closes at the same task.

Items carrying forward to phase 08 (recommended closure-targets):

- **I2 (Important; `serialize_response` unconditionally injects 5 standard headers — duplicate-header hazard).** `crates/envoy-admin/src/handler.rs:96-120` walks `resp.headers` writing them out, then *unconditionally* writes `cache-control: no-cache, max-age=0`, `x-content-type-options: nosniff`, `server: envoy-rust`, `date: <RFC 7231>`, `connection: close`. The current 06.1 endpoints (`render_ready`, `render_stats`, `render_stats_prometheus`, `render_404`, `render_405`) only set `content-type` / `content-length` / `allow` (where applicable) — so today the assumption holds and there are no duplicates. But the abstraction is fragile: a future endpoint that sets `cache-control: max-age=300` (e.g., a `/server_info` endpoint that's safe to cache briefly) would emit *both* headers on the wire. **Fix sketch**: in `serialize_response`, dedupe by case-insensitive header name before writing the standard headers — write only the ones not already present in `resp.headers`. ~10 LoC. **The current behavior is not a bug** for the 06.1 endpoint set; it's a latent maintenance hazard that will surface in phase 08 when the full admin endpoint surface (config_dump, clusters, listeners, runtime, server_info, /quitquitquit) lands. **Disposition: carry forward to phase 08.**
- **M1 (admin handler `resp.reason.unwrap_or("OK")` wrong for non-200 statuses).** `handler.rs:98` uses `unwrap_or("OK")` — if a future endpoint constructs a `Response { status: 404, reason: None, ... }`, the wire output is `HTTP/1.1 404 OK\r\n` which is wrong. All current 06.1 endpoints set `reason: Some(...)`, so the path is unreachable today. **Fix sketch**: map `unwrap_or` to the standard reason for the status code, or change `Response.reason` to non-Optional `String` and require renderer to populate. **Disposition: carry forward to phase 08 alongside I2** — same site (`serialize_response`); whichever phase first lands a `reason: None` arm. May fold into 06.2/06.3 if the access-log emitter happens to need a reason-from-status-code helper.
- **M4 (`DRAIN_BUDGET` constant duplicated between `envoy-admin` and `envoy-listener`).** `crates/envoy-admin/src/handler.rs:22` defines `DRAIN_BUDGET: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5)` and `crates/envoy-listener/src/lib.rs:135` defines the identical const inline. Two sources of truth for the same drain budget. Today the values agree; future drift would be silent. **Fix sketch**: hoist to `envoy-listener` and re-export, or add a `// keep in lockstep` comment at one or both sites. **Disposition: carry forward to phase 08** (graceful-drain consolidation).

Recommendations forward-track (per REVIEW §7):

- **R-1** — The dot-tree contract (`http.<stat_prefix>.downstream_rq_total = value-exact`; `cluster.<name>.upstream_cx_total = name-required, value-may-differ`; `listener.<name>.downstream_cx_total = value-exact`) is in BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md `Stat-name mapping` rows 1-3 as authoritative. 06.3's comprehensive stats wiring extends — each new stat lands a row with the `value-exact` or `name-required, value-may-differ` disposition + rationale. **Do NOT silently widen the allow-list in fixture 0011's expectations.yaml** when new counters are wired; widen the table first, allow-list second.
- **R-2** — The Prometheus exposition emitter's name-vs-label shape divergence (2 envoy-rust-only allow-list entries paired with their bare-name upstream-Envoy counterparts) is documented in BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md "06.1 Prometheus exposition shape divergence" subsection. When a later phase introduces a `StatsTagExtractor`-equivalent that projects dynamic name segments back into Prometheus labels, the 2 envoy-rust-only entries and their paired upstream-Envoy counterparts on the envoy-only side **must drop together as a single commit**. Half-dropping introduces a real divergence.
- **R-3** — `Driver::AdminScrape` and `BodyRule::PrometheusExposition` are reusable. 06.3 extends fixture 0011's `expectations.yaml` to assert the comprehensive stat set; the harness shape needs no change.
- **R-4** — The `connection: close` discipline on the admin response is a phase-08 generalization point. 06.1's admin handler closes the connection after each response (no keep-alive). Phase 08 may want HTTP/1.1 keep-alive for repeated scrapes from a Prometheus poller.
- **R-5** — The I2 `serialize_response` 5-header dedupe and the I1 idle-read-timeout should land before phase 08 expands the admin endpoint surface. 06.2 or 06.3 SPEC §6 should signpost both. Mechanical, ~20 LoC total.
- **R-6** — `Admin.access_log_path` is parsed-and-ignored at 06.1; admin-side access logging is OUT OF SCOPE in 06.2 too. The field stays parse-and-ignored indefinitely from 06.1; if 06.3 or a later phase wires admin-side access logging, the field already exists in the schema and `AdminConfig` already carries it through — no migration needed.
- **R-7** — The HCM stat-prefix-namespacing pattern (`format!("http.{stat_prefix}.<name>", ...)`) is the convention. 06.3 extends with `..._2xx`, `..._3xx`, `..._4xx`, `..._5xx`, and (per Rule 4) `..._access_logs_total`. Use the same `format!` pattern; register at `HCMStats::register` time; expose via `HCMStats` field accessors. The `register` method is idempotent for same-kind so re-registration of the same stat under the same `stat_prefix` is safe.
- **R-8** — The `Counter::add(n)` API exists but is unused by 06.1's three counters. When 06.3 wires bulk-increment paths (e.g., `bytes_received`/`bytes_sent` counters that increment per-N-bytes rather than per-event), `add(n)` is the right primitive; `inc()` would be wrong. The API is in place; usage starts in 06.3 if the bytes-side counters land then.
- **R-9** — Pre-state-4 fmt discipline. The 06.1 Task 14 fmt-drift catch (13 files of accumulated drift across Tasks 2-13) is the precedent: per-task PROGRESS sections logged "clippy clean" but not "fmt clean," and the drift accumulated quietly. 06.2 / 06.3 / future phases should consider running `cargo fmt --all -- --check` at every PROGRESS-task close, not just at state-4. Or land a pre-commit hook (out of scope for in-phase work; signposts for a future infra-only phase if anyone scopes it).

- **R-5** — The Task 6 follow-up pattern (review-fix landing as a small dedicated commit between Task 6 and Task 7) is a precedent worth preserving. `f73face` lands a single-issue fix (gate `from_file_for_test` behind `#[cfg(feature = "test-util")]`) as a named "Task 6 follow-up" commit with its own PROGRESS section. This contrasts with the 06.1 Task 11 follow-up commit (`6b957ae`) that restored admin headers. Both demonstrate that mid-execution review-fixups land cleanly as small named commits, not amendments to the original task — D-3.5 / D-3.6 in action.
- **R-6** — The bind-mount-parent-directory CI-fix shape (`tests/differential/src/lib.rs:1374-1432`) should be inherited by any future writable-mount fixture. PROGRESS Task 11 "Carry-to-REVIEW.md notes" flags this: *"Linux Docker bind-mount file-level mode bits don't reliably propagate write permissions; mount a parent directory at 0o777 and let the in-container process create the file fresh."* 06.3 D17.3's fixture-0011-comprehensive-stats extension doesn't add new writable mounts (stats endpoints are read-only), so 06.3 itself doesn't need the pattern — but the future phase that first adds a writable mount (e.g., access-log + gRPC ALS sink fixtures, RTDS file-source phases) should consult the in-tree comment first.
- **R-7** — A pre-push parity gate (running CI Docker locally on Linux, or `act` on the workflow) would have caught the cross-Docker bind-mount issue at state-3 rather than state-4. PROGRESS Task 11 "Carry-to-REVIEW.md notes" raises this. Out of 06.3 scope (it's a CI-infra concern), but worth signposting in a future infra-only phase.
- **R-8** — The `BodyRule::ByteExact` extension (M2) should land alongside whichever phase next surfaces a fixture-specific body assertion need.
- **R-9** — The `Http1Error::AccessLogOpen { message: String }` vs `StatsRegistration { stat_prefix, message: String }` pattern should be reconciled in whichever phase next refactors typed-error chains.
- **R-10** — The `upstream_service_time` extraction reads from the captured `response_headers_for_log`, NOT from the live response. `crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs` explicitly pushes the `x-envoy-upstream-service-time` header into `response_headers_for_log` so the dispatch site's `extract_upstream_service_time` helper can observe it (since the live downstream wire output is already consumed). 06.3 should re-verify this when the router-proxy fixture (whichever first exercises the upstream-service-time access-log field) lands; today fixture 0012's direct_response path emits `-` for this token on both sides and the integration is structurally exercised but not asserted.

- **ADR-0023** (`ClusterType::StrictDns` accepted; `LOGICAL_DNS` deferred) — landed at 05.1 Task 1 commit `bfabcb6` (inline at Task 1 per the ADR-0021 inline-at-Task-1 precedent). Closes phase-02.1 REVIEW I3 (positive `Static` regression guard, enabled by introducing the second `ClusterType` variant). **Partially closes phase-04.3 REVIEW C-1** (cross-phase Docker-gated regression — the original Envoy v1.33 `malformed IP address: host.docker.internal` startup error is no longer triggered; fixture 0008's residual upstream-routing defect closed substantively in 05.4).
- **ADR-0024** (`Cluster.dns_lookup_family` field + `DnsLookupFamily` enum in envoy-config; parse-only with runtime non-consumption deliberate) — landed at 05.4 Task 1 commit `3d0af4a` (inline at Task 1 per the ADR-0021 / ADR-0023 inline-at-Task-1 precedent). The 3-variant enum (V4Only / V6Only / Auto) is the minimum viable coverage of Envoy v1.33's surface; runtime non-consumption is doctrine-correct per D-3.6 minimalism (the runtime-extension trigger is named: "whichever later phase first needs envoy-rust to filter resolved addresses by family lands the runtime extension then, with its own test"). Substantively closes phase-04.3 REVIEW C-1's IPv6/IPv4 selection regression at the upstream Envoy boundary (when paired with Task 2's 5-fixture YAML edit setting `dns_lookup_family: V4_ONLY` on the `host.docker.internal` clusters).
- **ADR-0026** (`Listener.listener_filters: Vec<serde_yaml::Value>` parse-and-ignore field in envoy-config — NEW PATTERN) — landed at 05.4 Task 3 commit `f1dbe12`. Enables envoy.yaml fixtures to declare listener filters that envoy-rust does NOT execute (envoy-rust performs SNI dispatch at the rustls layer; phase 03.2 architectural choice). The `Vec<serde_yaml::Value>` opaque-storage type preserves the ability to inspect without typing. Enables fixture 0006's explicit `tls_inspector` block needed on macOS Docker. **Bounds future extension explicitly**: "Whichever later phase first needs to ACTUALLY EXECUTE a listener filter lands a typed-variant extension on the field plus a runtime dispatch arm — not a new ADR (extending an existing pattern)."
- **ADR-0025** (suppress synthetic `content-length: 0` on empty-body requests in `envoy-http1::Client` per RFC 7230 §3.3.2 + Envoy v1.33 parity) — landed at 05.4 Task 5 commit `01edie3`. Pass-through unchanged for explicit Content-Length AND for non-empty bodies; suppression triggers only when the body is `None` or empty `&[]`. Closes phase-04.3 REVIEW C-1's fixture-0008 byte-equal-echo regression (upstream Envoy was returning the synthetic `content-length: 0` line in the deterministic-echo body, which the differential gate rejected as a byte mismatch). 05.3's H2 codec emission decision should reference this ADR + the `body_is_nonempty` predicate per REVIEW §4 R-4.
- **ADR-0027** (`http` crate (`http::Request` / `http::Response` / `http::HeaderMap`) typed-surface scoping — `http` graduates from transitive-only via `h2` to a direct workspace foundation, scoped narrowly to `envoy-http2`'s codec-edge translations) — landed at 05.2 Task 1 commit `9c2b2fd` (inline at Task 1 alongside the `crates/envoy-http2/Cargo.toml` scaffold creation, per the ADR-0021 / ADR-0023 / ADR-0024 inline-at-Task-1 precedent). Mirrors ADR-0021's `regex` scoping discipline. Renumbering provenance: projected as conditional ADR-0024 in 05.2 SPEC §7 + parent-05 SPEC §7; renumbered to ADR-0027 at landing time because phase 05.4 landed ADR-0024 / ADR-0025 / ADR-0026 between SPEC writeup and 05.2 execution. Mirrors the phase-03 ADR-renumbering precedent.
- **ADR-0028** (resolution of the `envoy-http1` ↔ `envoy-http2` cycle introduced by 05.3 SPEC §3 D4 router dispatch) — landed at 05.3 Task 6 commit `366af8b`. **Documented D-3.5 in-execution deviation from 05.3 SPEC §7's "no new ADRs projected" projection.** The cycle was discovered when the controller attempted to add `envoy-http2` as a `[dependencies]` entry on `crates/envoy-http1/Cargo.toml` to wire the H1 router-arm dispatch — `envoy-http2` already depends on `envoy-http1` for the listener-side `HCMConfig` type alias landed in 05.2, so adding the reverse edge would create a Cargo cycle. The ADR adopts option (B) — deferral: the H1 router-arm at `crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs`'s `BuildOutcome::Proxy` does not dispatch to H2 clusters in 05.3; the cluster's `upstream_protocol` field is queried but the H1 path returns a 502 with a doctrine-line body when the cluster is `Http2`-flagged. The H2 router-arm dispatch lives at `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs` and dispatches symmetrically to either H1 or H2 clusters via the new `envoy-http2::Client`. Future-extension trigger: option (A) — extract a third crate `envoy-http-router` carrying the protocol-agnostic router-walk + `BuildOutcome` + dispatch — is the natural close site if a future phase needs cross-protocol cluster sharing on the H1 listener. **Bounds future extension explicitly**: "Whichever later phase first needs the H1-listener × H2-cluster path lands the `envoy-http-router` extraction; this ADR's option-(B) deferral is then superseded by reference."

- **M3 (Minor; fixture 0013's `expected_body` byte-exact assertion coupled to upstream Envoy's request-header injection set).** `tests/fixtures/0013-http-filter-header-mutation/expectations.yaml` hardcodes the exact echoed header set; this relies on `envoy.yaml`'s `request_headers_to_remove` block enumerating every header Envoy v1.33 injects (the same posture as fixture 0008). Correct today (CI run `25887571566` green) but a future Envoy version-pin bump that adds a new default request header would silently break the body-exact assertion. The coupling is documented in the fixture `README.md` but not at the assertion site. **Fix sketch:** add a cross-reference comment in `expectations.yaml`. **Disposition: close opportunistically** — natural forced-close site is the future `ENVOY_TARGET.md` version-bump phase (its own phase per D-3.7) that re-baselines the differential suite.

Named owner: 08.2 or later harness-touch phase.

Items carrying forward (the 8 Minor M1-M8 + 3 test/audit-trail T1-T3 findings — all awareness-only / close-opportunistically; **none has a hard-gated owner phase; none gated the 08.2 state-6 close-out**):

- **M1 (Minor; `let drain = async { … };` local shadows `drain: Arc<DrainState>` parameter in `Listener::serve`).** `crates/envoy-listener/src/lib.rs:323` declares a local `drain` future for the post-loop drain-wait block, shadowing the `drain: Arc<DrainState>` parameter at line 241. **Why it matters:** D-3.4 stranger-readability — a future maintainer adding code between the select and the post-loop block would see `drain` resolve unexpectedly. **Fix sketch:** rename the local to `drain_join` or `drain_fut` (~1-line edit). **Disposition: close opportunistically** at the next phase that touches `Listener::serve`. Named owner: future hardening or filter-family phase that extends the select. Non-blocking.
- **M2 (Minor; `Err(0)` sentinel in `drain()`'s second-CAS-skip branch collides semantically with `DrainStage::Live as u8` discriminant).** `crates/envoy-listener/src/drain.rs:204` reads `Err(0) // Sentinel — we already succeeded via from_live.`. The `0` value happens to be the `DrainStage::Live` discriminant; functionally fine because only `.is_ok()` is checked at line 206, but a reader could mis-read the encoding. **Fix sketch:** either (a) use `Err(u8::MAX)` as a sentinel that cannot collide + extend the comment, OR (b) refactor to a single boolean expression collapsing the conditional (~2-5 LoC). **Disposition: close opportunistically** at the next phase that touches `drain.rs`. Named owner: future drain-time-config phase or feature-family extension. Non-blocking.
- **M3 (Minor; BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md "Admin-action effect equivalence" rows for `/healthcheck/fail` + `/healthcheck/ok` claim "100ms" wire-flip budget unenforced).** `docs/envoy-rust/BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md:163-164` carries `"Both proxies MUST flip /ready to 503 within 100ms"`. The 100ms budget is doctrinal — `fail_healthcheck()` / `ok_healthcheck()` are synchronous `compare_exchange` + gauge updates + nothing else (sub-microsecond on a non-loaded host), but no test or fixture measures the latency or enforces the bound. **Fix sketch:** either (a) downgrade the row prose to `"synchronously observable after the POST response completes"` (~2 LoC contract edit), OR (b) add a `MaxLatencyMs` assertion type to the harness + a fixture or test that bounds the flip latency (sizable; defer indefinitely). Recommendation: option (a). **Disposition: close opportunistically** at the next phase that touches BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT's "Admin-action effect equivalence" subsection. Named owner: future healthcheck-filter phase or operations-hardening phase. Non-blocking; doc-tightening only.
- **M4 (Minor; `empty_200_ok()` helper omits `content-type` entirely).** `crates/envoy-admin/src/endpoint.rs:570-577` constructs `Response { status: 200, reason: Some("OK"), headers: [("content-length", "0")], body: Bytes::new() }` — no `content-type` header. RFC 7231 §3.1.1.5 permits this for empty bodies; upstream Envoy v1.33's `/drain_listeners` empirically carries `content-type: text/plain`. Fixture 0015 does NOT assert on `/drain_listeners`'s `content-type` (the scrape is `/server_info`). **Fix sketch:** add `("content-type", "text/plain")` to the headers vec at `endpoint.rs:572` (~1 LoC). **Disposition: close opportunistically** at whichever future phase first adds a POST-endpoint response-header assertion fixture. Named owner: future POST-endpoint header-assertion phase. Non-blocking; upstream-parity polish only.
- **M5 (Minor; `drain_signal()` always heap-allocates via `Box::pin`).** `crates/envoy-listener/src/drain.rs:246, 248` returns `Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = ()> + Send + '_>>` — the dynamic-dispatch return shape is forced by the two-arm return type asymmetry (`std::future::ready(())` vs `Notified<'_>`). The `Box::pin` allocates on every `drain_signal()` call (once per listener-accept-loop iteration). Under MVP-scale fixture load the cost is trivial; under high QPS this would become a per-connection allocation. **Fix sketch:** convert to `pub async fn drain_signal(&self)` + an internal `enum DrainSignalFuture<'a> { Ready, Pending(Notified<'a>) }` implementing `Future` (~20-30 LoC; mechanical). **Disposition: carry forward indefinitely** — activates only if a future high-throughput deployment surfaces allocator pressure on the accept loop's drain-signal path. Named owner: whichever future phase first benchmarks the accept loop's allocator footprint. Non-blocking; forward-looking performance note only.
- **M6 (Minor; `admin_handler_new_6arg_tests::admin_handler_new_accepts_six_args_and_constructs` test name + module name now describe a 7-arg shape post-Task-4 widening).** `crates/envoy-admin/src/handler.rs:953-985` retains the 06.1-era test name + module name despite Task 4's 7-arg widening. **Why it matters:** D-3.4 stranger-readability — a future maintainer searching for "6arg" tests would find this misnamed surface. **Fix sketch:** rename module to `admin_handler_new_constructor_tests` + test to `admin_handler_new_accepts_arg_count_and_constructs` + trim the 70-line block comment to a 3-line note pointing at the sibling Task-4 coverage (~75-line edit). **Disposition: close opportunistically** at the next phase that touches `crates/envoy-admin/src/handler.rs::tests`. Named owner: future admin-endpoint extension or test-organization cleanup pass. Non-blocking.
- **M7 (Minor; `drain_signal()` doc-comment "tens of microseconds" claim is unmeasured).** `crates/envoy-admin/src/endpoint.rs:531-535` (and a similar phrasing in `drain.rs` doc-comments) carries the claim that `notify_waiters → listener-serve-drop-listener` latency is "tens of microseconds" on Linux/macOS loopback. Structurally plausible but no benchmark or measurement is cited. **Fix sketch:** either (a) drop the quantification (`"sub-millisecond on a non-loaded host"`) OR (b) back with a `tokio::time::Instant` measurement in `serve_returns_when_drain_signal_fires`. Recommendation: option (a) (~1-line edit). **Disposition: close opportunistically** at the next phase that touches `endpoint.rs::render_drain_listeners`. Named owner: future admin-action-surface extension phase. Non-blocking; doc-tightening only.
- **M8 (Minor; `AdminEndpoint::render`'s `Ready` arm at `endpoint.rs:163-168` is `unreachable!()`).** The registry-only `render` path 08.1 D6 introduced cannot serve handler-scoped endpoints; the `Ready` arm reads `unreachable!("Ready requires handler-scoped DrainState; dispatch via AdminEndpoint::render_with")`. The `render_with` dispatch at `endpoint.rs:194-200` correctly routes `Ready` through `render_ready_with(handler)`, so the `render` arm is genuinely unreachable in production. A future maintainer adding a registry-only dispatch site for `Ready` would hit a runtime panic rather than getting a compile error. The same concern applies to `ConfigDump` / `ServerInfo` / `Clusters` / `Listeners` arms (all handler-scoped + `unreachable!()` in `render`). **Fix sketch:** split `AdminEndpoint` into `enum AdminEndpoint { Registry(RegistryEndpoint), Handler(HandlerEndpoint) }` with separate render fns (~150 LoC; sizable typestate refactor). **Disposition: carry forward indefinitely** — activates only if a future feature requires registry-only dispatch of a currently-handler-scoped endpoint. Named owner: whichever future phase first introduces a synthetic-state admin endpoint requiring registry-only dispatch. Non-blocking; type-safety refactor opportunity only.

- **First filter pick: `envoy.filters.http.local_ratelimit`.** Picked directly per `feedback_pick_recommendation`. Per the §9 HTTP-filter sub-feature enumeration (header_mutation DONE at 07.2), considered 14 candidate filters along (config shape / foundations needed / framework extension needed):

  - **local_rate_limit (WINNER)** — filter-chain config; no per-route required; zero foundations (hand-roll token bucket via std-lib atomic + Mutex); zero framework extension (Decision::StopAndSend exists from 07.1).
  - cors — per-route CorsPolicy via typed_per_filter_config is primary; rejected — needs new per-route framework primitive.
  - fault — needs `rand` for percentage sampling (deterministic-only scope loses upstream parity); rejected — random sampling forces foundations grant.
  - buffer — tiny config (max_request_bytes); rejected — needs new body-buffering framework extension (larger than the filter itself).
  - csrf — per-route primary; same per-route extension as cors; rejected.
  - compression — needs `flate2`/`brotli`/`zstd` foundations grant + new pluggable-compressor primitive; rejected.
  - rbac — medium principal-matcher primitive; rejected (medium scope).
  - adaptive concurrency — sophisticated gradient-based algorithm; rejected (algorithm-heavy).
  - jwt_authn — needs `jsonwebtoken` foundations grant + JOSE primitive; rejected.
  - ext_authz / ext_proc — needs gRPC client + cross-process call protocol; rejected (depends on gRPC family).
  - oauth2 — needs HTTPS client + auth-state framework; rejected.
  - admission control — probabilistic + stats-heavy (P50/P99); rejected.
  - bandwidth limit — per-stream timing; rejected.
  - global rate limit — needs gRPC client + RLS protocol; rejected (depends on gRPC family).
  - lua / wasm — scripting hosts; own multi-phase sub-projects per §9; rejected.

  Top-3 viable: local_rate_limit > fault > buffer. **local_rate_limit wins** on: pure filter-chain config (no per-route extension); validates `Decision::StopAndSend(FilterResponse)` path with non-trivial 429 + `x-envoy-ratelimited` response shape (fixture 0013 / header_mutation only exercised `Decision::Continue`); 4-counter stat surface matching upstream Envoy v1.33 parity exactly; deterministic semantics (no `rand` foundations grant); no new top-level Cargo deps; ~900-1100 LoC including tests + fixture. **Mid-execution discovery + ADR-0033 corrective sequence (4 commits over Tasks 5-7).**

Task 5 dispatch (the Docker-gated differential fixture authoring step) surfaced 3 SPEC §2.2 + Task 3 lock-in #13 discrepancies against upstream Envoy v1.33's actual `envoy.filters.http.local_ratelimit` wire shape per empirical Docker observation:

1. **Upstream does NOT emit `x-envoy-ratelimited` from local_ratelimit** (that header belongs to the global ratelimit filter + router-side response-flag handling per upstream v1.33 source).
2. **Upstream's 429 body is the source-hardcoded `"local_rate_limited"` (18 bytes)**, not empty (the upstream proto has no configurable `response_body` field).
3. **envoy-rust's H1 HCM filter-StopAndSend writer-path skips standard-header decoration** — the synth-from-build paths (`synth_status`, `synth_direct_response`) populate the 5 standard HTTP/1.1 response headers inline; the filter-synth path (`RequestPath::SynthFromDecode` arm + encode-side `Decision::StopAndSend` arm) takes `filter_resp.headers` verbatim. A latent 07.x framework defect that 07.2 HeaderMutation never exposed (HeaderMutation's `decode_headers` returns `Decision::Continue` unconditionally — the filter only mutates header lists, never short-circuits); phase 09's LocalRateLimit is the first production filter to surface the gap.

Items carrying forward (the 3 Minor M1-M3 + 2 doc-staleness D1-D2 + 3 test/audit-trail T1-T3 findings — all awareness-only / close-opportunistically; **none has a hard-gated owner phase; none gated the 09 state-6 close-out**):

- **M1 (Minor; `TokenBucketState::try_acquire` CAS-shape race on the refill path).** `crates/envoy-filter/src/local_rate_limit.rs:215-287` — the CAS at line 263 reads `compare_exchange(current, next, ...)` where `current = self.tokens.load(...)` (pre-refill value) and `next = available - 1`. When `available = current + 1` (exactly one interval elapsed AND `tokens_per_fill = 1`), `next` collapses to `current`, making the CAS `compare_exchange(current, current)` — which succeeds unconditionally for any concurrent thread observing the same `current`. Two threads observing the same `current` value in this scenario both succeed their CAS, both return `true`, and the single refill token is "consumed" twice. **Why it matters:** real concurrent double-consumption bug on the refill path. **Why it does NOT rise above Minor at phase-09 scope:** the bug is exercised only when `tokens_per_fill > 0` AND a refill interval elapses concurrently with multiple acquires AND the refill credit per interval is exactly enough to bridge `current → current + 1`. Phase 09's actual exercise paths all avoid the contested arm (fixture 0016 uses `tokens_per_fill: 3` + `fill_interval: 60s` with sub-1s burst; backstop uses `tokens_per_fill: 2` + 60s same shape; torture test uses `tokens_per_fill: 0`). The token cap at `max_tokens` provides a hard ceiling on over-crediting — blast radius bounded. **Fix sketch:** either (a) require `available > current` precondition for the CAS, OR (b) replace `compare_exchange(current, next)` with a token-decrement loop that re-loads on every iteration AND atomically combines the refill-credit with the consume. ~15-30 LoC + an additional torture test exercising the contested path. **Disposition: close at whichever future HTTP-filter-family phase first exercises non-zero `tokens_per_fill` within a refill-window-spanning burst**, OR at a dedicated token-bucket hardening pass. Named owner: future HTTP-filter-family phase (likely global-rate-limit or fault-injection). Non-blocking.

- **M2 (Minor; H2 HCM writer-arm sites don't decorate filter-synth responses with standard HTTP/1.1 response headers; ADR-0033 Consequences misrepresents this as "H2 naturally inherits").** `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:373-378` (decode-side `H2RequestPath::SynthFromDecode`) returns the filter's response verbatim; `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:436-443` (encode-side `Decision::StopAndSend(replacement)`) constructs `resp` verbatim; both pass through `build_http_response` at `crates/envoy-http2/src/response.rs:29-50` which does NOT add `server` / `date` / `content-type`. An H2 listener exercising the phase-09 LocalRateLimitFilter would emit 429 responses missing those standard headers (the H2-forbidden `connection` correctly stays stripped; `content-length` is implicit from `send_data(end_of_stream=true)`). ADR-0033 Consequences §iii(c)-end (`docs/envoy-rust/DECISIONS.md` ~line 697) claims "the corresponding H2 HCM path naturally inherits via the shared Http1HCMConfig re-export" — but this conflates config re-export with code reuse (H2 writer-arm sites have their own response-construction code that does NOT call `decorate_filter_synth_response`). Will mislead future filter-family phases (fault / ext_authz / oauth2 / rbac) into assuming H2 is already covered. **Why it does NOT rise above Minor at phase-09 scope:** the phase-09 differential surface is HTTP/1.1 only (fixture 0016's `codec_type: HTTP1`); the in-process backstop is HTTP/1.1 only; the H2 gap is genuinely latent and unexercised by phase-09's actual bilateral assertion. **Fix sketch:** either (a) amend ADR-0033 Consequences + PROGRESS Commit C forward-looking note to explicitly record the H2 analogous gap as known-deferred (~10-15 LoC docs edit; preferred per parent-08 SPEC §6.1 alternative (vi) accept-drift), OR (b) land an H2 `decorate_filter_synth_response` analogue (~50-70 LoC + 2 tests; extends the corrective sequence by 1 commit). **Disposition: prefer (a); close at next HTTP-filter-family phase exercising filters on H2** (fault / ext_authz / oauth2 / rbac per ADR-0033 Consequences §5). Named owner: future HTTP-filter-family phase exercising filters on H2. Non-blocking.

- **M3 (Minor; Task 7 in-process backstop subprocess discipline regresses from 07.2 / 08.2 precedents).** `crates/envoy-bin/tests/http_filter_local_rate_limit.rs:30` declares `use std::process::{Command, Stdio};` (no `kill_on_drop` API); lines 180-188 configure `.stderr(Stdio::piped()).stdout(Stdio::piped())` (both pipes; no concurrent drain reader). 07.2 + 08.2 backstops both use `tokio::process::Command` + `kill_on_drop(true)` + `Stdio::null()` for stdout. **Why it matters:** (a) any panic in `send_request_and_collect`'s 8 `.expect(...)` / `.unwrap()` sites before explicit `child.kill()` leaks the envoy-bin subprocess; (b) un-drained stdout pipe doubles the OS-pipe-buffer-fill deadlock surface; (c) PROGRESS Task 7's "same pattern as 07.2 backstop" claim is factually wrong — the discipline is a regression from BOTH 07.2 AND 08.2. **Why it does NOT rise above Minor at phase-09 scope:** test-helper-only; no production-code impact; the state-4 CI anchor ran the backstop GREEN with no leaks observed (the test passed cleanly so no panic sites fired); the CI environment's process-lifecycle cleanup mitigates the leak risk on green-test runs. **Fix sketch:** 3-line patch: `use tokio::process::{Command, Stdio};` + `.stdout(Stdio::null())` + `.kill_on_drop(true)`. ~3 LoC; trivially mechanical. **Disposition: close at next HTTP-filter-family phase touching `crates/envoy-bin/tests/http_filter_*.rs` backstops**, OR opportunistically. Named owner: future HTTP-filter-family phase touching backstops. Non-blocking; test-helper-only.

The implementation is correct (the encode-side decoration site is the `envoy_filter::Decision::StopAndSend(replacement) =>` arm of the encode-side filter dispatch, NOT a separate `SynthFromEncode` variant of `RequestPath`); only the ADR / PROGRESS prose uses fictional variant names; the line-number references are correct. **Disposition: no action; close opportunistically** at whichever future ADR amends or references ADR-0033 (likely never — ADRs are append-only). Named owner: none. Awareness-only narrative cleanup.

- **T1 (Minor; Task 1 `parse_duration` accepts `+`-prefixed numeric values silently).** `crates/envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs:1825-1842` — `u64::from_str` accepts `"+60"`, `"0060s"`, and similar non-canonical shapes that upstream Envoy v1.33's protobuf Duration parser would reject. No test covers `"+60s"` or `"-1s"`. **Why it does NOT rise above Minor:** the validator at `validate_local_rate_limit_config` runs after parse and rejects bogus durations (`fill_interval > 0` check); a `+60s` input would produce a `Duration` of 60s and behave identically to `60s`. Action-vs-match decision matrix per SPEC §5.6: `Allow+match → ALLOW`, `Allow+no_match → DENY`, `Deny+match → DENY`, `Deny+no_match → ALLOW`. The `connection: close` appears because the harness sends `Connection: close` per `drive_http_get` at line 1039; if a client sends keep-alive (or default HTTP/1.1 keep-alive), upstream omits `connection` (verified with `curl -i` default — observed 4 headers, no `connection`). envoy-rust's `decorate_filter_synth_response` helper adds the same 5 headers under the harness framing. **No SPEC revision needed.**

  - **fault — abort path (WINNER)** — StopAndSend-capable (abort short-circuits via 503); ZERO foundations (reuses StopAndSend + the H1 helper template + 04.2 HeaderMatcher; `FractionalPercent` is a small hand-authored envoy-config type); the ONLY genuinely new surface is the bounded H2 `decorate_filter_synth_response_h2` helper (the 09 M2 close); the deterministic 0%/100% abort path is fully differential-testable; ~1350-1500 LoC under the §6.1 gate. The documented phase-10 runner-up. Scoped to abort-only; **fractional percentage + delay + response_rate_limit + grpc_status + downstream-controlled faults + max_active_faults defer per SPEC §4** — notably fractional percentage defers because a per-request probabilistic abort decision is **non-differential-testable** (the differential contract §7.2 does not compare probabilistic per-request outcomes across two independent proxies), and delay defers because timing is not compared by default per §7.2.
  - **jwt_authn (reject → 401)** — StopAndSend-capable + would close 09 M2 if exercised on H2; but needs a JOSE/`jsonwebtoken` foundations grant + JWKS-fetch framework. Rejected on foundation-pressure.
  - **cors (preflight → 200/204)** — StopAndSend-capable for OPTIONS preflight; but CORS is primary per-route in upstream Envoy → needs the per-route framework extension (a ~200-300 LoC gating primitive). Rejected on arch-risk; CORS remains the natural per-route-config close site per the family-wide deferral.
  - **csrf (reject → 403)** — per-route primary; same per-route extension as cors. Rejected.
  - **oauth2 (redirect)** — needs an HTTPS client + auth-state framework. Rejected.
  - **ext_authz / ext_proc** — need a gRPC client (depends on the gRPC family). Rejected.
  - **buffer / bandwidth_limit / compression / response-rate-limit** — need a body-buffering/streaming framework extension larger than the filter. Rejected.
  - **global rate limit** — depends on the gRPC family. Rejected.
  - **adaptive concurrency / admission control** — sophisticated + probabilistic/stats-heavy; non-differential-testable core. Rejected.
  - **lua / wasm** — own multi-phase sub-projects per §9. Rejected.

  Top-3 viable: **fault (abort) > jwt_authn > cors.** **fault (abort) wins** on: zero foundations grant; the lowest-risk vehicle for the 09 M2 H2-decoration close; deterministic abort fully differential-testable; ~1350-1500 LoC under the §6.1 gate. The SPEC §3 D6 records the H2 decoration helper (the centerpiece); SPEC §6.2 makes the empirical verification at state-2 PLAN-write REQUIRED for the fault stats namespace + abort body bytes + H2 abort header set against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (the phase-10-ratified verify-at-PLAN-write process improvement).

- **Scope-cut decision (fractional percentage deferral):** Picked directly per `feedback_pick_recommendation`. Phase 11 supports **deterministic 0%/100% percentage only**; the validator rejects fractional (`0 < numerator < denominator`) per SPEC §4 + §5.6. **Rationale:** a fractional per-request abort decision depends on a random draw that cannot be matched across two independent proxies, so it is non-differential-testable per the differential contract §7.2; landing it would be untested (un-differential-verifiable) code per `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §6.3. Deferring it (a) keeps phase 11 entirely inside the differential contract, (b) avoids landing a hand-rolled per-request PRNG that no fixture can exercise bilaterally, and (c) keeps the phase under the §6.1 gate. The deterministic 0%/100% path needs no PRNG. Fractional defers to a future fault-enrichment phase that hand-rolls the PRNG per D-3.2 + opts into statistical-distribution unit testing per §7.2 (consistent with the rbac "header-based scope only; IP/CIDR defers" minimum-viable-cut discipline at phase 10).

- **Phase id + slug pick:** **`11`** / **`11-http-filter-fault`**. The id `11` is next sequential after `10` per the project's numbering convention (the next standalone-phase id is the next integer; sub-phases get `.N` suffixes only on split). The slug mirrors the `10-http-filter-rbac` + `09-http-filter-local-rate-limit` hyphenation pattern — readable English (`http-filter-fault`) over the upstream-name verbatim. The filter's typed_config `name:` field uses upstream's exact `envoy.filters.http.fault` (typed_config `@type` `…fault.v3.HTTPFault`); the slug + readable name + upstream config name are deliberately distinct surfaces per the 07.2 / 09 / 10 precedent.

Per `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §9 depends-on doctrine (HTTP-filter-family extensions name `07`). **An implicit dependency on phase `05` (the HTTP/2 codec + `Driver::Http2` harness primitive) is load-bearing for the first time in the HTTP-filter family** (phase 11's fixture runs on an H2 listener) — but per ROADMAP schema conventions only direct ROADMAP-row deps are captured in the field; cross-deliverable reuse (05 H2 codec, 04.2 HeaderMatcher, 09 H1 helper template) is implicit. ### Phase-12 state-2 split decision

This subsection records the phase-12 state-2 PLAN-write commit (`phase 12: state-2 split decision + sub-phase SPECs (12.1/12.2) [ADR-0036, ADR-0037]`) — the fifth project SPLIT state-2 (after phases 02/03/07/08), all per the user's standing preferences `feedback_pick_recommendation` (pick the recommendation; no two-option fork) + `feedback_execution_style` (the state-2 PLAN-write is the controller's authoring pass; subagent-driven execution applies at state 3). Docs-only; 5 files; ADR-0036 (split) + ADR-0037 (no-healthy-body reconciliation); no SPEC edit to the parent-12 SPEC; no PLAN/PROGRESS (those land at the 12.1 state-2 PLAN-write next session).

**§6.2 empirical-verification findings (HEAVY; 6 items; against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`).** Performed at THIS commit by the controller directly (per the parent SPEC §6.2 + the phase-10/11-ratified verify-at-PLAN-write discipline). Methodology: a Docker bridge network with (a) a synthetic health-aware backend container (returns 200 on `/`, a configurable status on `/healthz`, logs every probe) and (b) an `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` container running an active-HC cluster pointing at the backend by container name (STRICT_DNS); admin `/stats` scraped + data-plane `GET /` probed across the convergence window. *(Initial host-networking attempts via `host.docker.internal` network-failed because it resolves IPv6-only on this Docker Desktop; resolved by co-locating both containers on a shared bridge network.)*

| # | Item | Finding | Disposition |
|---|------|---------|-------------|
| 1 | **Initial endpoint health state** (the single most load-bearing) | **Unhealthy/pending-until-first-pass.** An unhealthy backend with a 3 s probe delay → data-plane `no healthy upstream` (503) from t=0, *before* the first probe resolves. Hosts with active HC configured begin not-healthy; the first passing check (`healthy_threshold` consecutive successes) marks them healthy. | **MATCHES** the parent SPEC's recommended projection. Drives D3 (`EndpointHealth` initial state = Unhealthy) + the 12.1 inert-and-unexercised-seam note. No ADR. |
| 2 | **No-healthy-upstream synth body** (the byte-precision item) | status **503**; body **`no healthy upstream`** = **19 bytes**, hex `6e 6f 20 68 65 61 6c 74 68 79 20 75 70 73 74 72 65 61 6d`, **no trailing newline**; headers `{ content-length:19, content-type:text/plain, date, server:envoy, connection:close }`; **no wire `x-envoy-*` flag header**. | **DIVERGES from envoy-rust's existing synth-503** (`hcm.rs:918 synth_status` = EMPTY body, content-length:0). → **ADR-0037**: reconcile envoy-rust to emit the 19-byte body on the no-healthy-upstream path (impl in 12.2 D6.2, only the `hcm.rs:582` arm — NOT global `synth_status`). Fixture 0019 asserts byte-exact. |
| 3 | **Panic threshold** | default **50 %**; comparison **strictly-below** (`healthy% < threshold`: `value:0` → `0%<0%`=false → no panic → 503; default 50 % → `0%<50%`=true → panic → 200 routed to all); `Percent` shape **`{ value: <double> }`**; panic = round-robin over ALL; bonus stat `cluster.<n>.lb_healthy_panic` (not wired at phase-12 scope). | **MATCHES** projection. Drives D1 (`CommonLbConfig`/`Percent`) + D5 (panic logic). Fixture uses `{ value: 0 }` (disable panic). No ADR. |
| 4 | **Health-check stat names** | `cluster.<n>.health_check.{attempt,success,failure,passive_failure,network_failure,verify_cluster,healthy,degraded}` + `membership_{healthy,total,degraded,excluded,change}`. `membership_healthy` = count of currently-healthy endpoints (1 healthy / 0 ejected). | **MATCHES** projection. 12.1 wires the minimum-viable subset: `attempt`/`success`/`failure` counters + `membership_healthy` gauge (rest defer per parent §4). No ADR. |
| 5 | **HTTP probe shape** | `GET /healthz`, `:authority`/`Host: <cluster-name>` (default when `http_health_check.host` unset), `user-agent: Envoy/HC`; default `expected_statuses` = **exactly 200** (201 → unhealthy); `Int64Range` **half-open `[start, end)`** (`[200,201)` excludes 201; `[200,202)` includes it — reusable directly). | **MATCHES** projection. Drives D1 (`HttpHealthCheck`) + D4 (probe). No ADR. |
| 6 | **Duration config shape** | Envoy accepts decimal-second protobuf-JSON durations (`1s`/`0.5s`/`0.25s`) but **REJECTS `500ms`**; envoy-rust's `parse_duration` accepts `1s`/`500ms`/`500us` (integer + s/ms/us) but **REJECTS `0.5s`** (parses the numeric part as `u64`). **Shared form = integer seconds only.** | **DIVERGES from the parent SPEC fixture sketch's `interval: 0.5s`** (which envoy-rust would reject). → **PLAN-time correction (no ADR):** the 12.2 fixture uses integer-second durations (`interval: 1s`, `timeout: 1s`) on both sides (identical YAMLs); 12.1 reuses `parse_duration` as-is (no `0.5s` support added — scope creep). |

**Disposition:** items 1/3/4/5 MATCHED → no ADR. Item 2 → **ADR-0037** (the load-bearing wire-level body bytes pinned; the ADR-0034-class durability decision; reconcile-by-implementation per D-3.3). Item 6 → PLAN-time fixture-shape correction (no ADR). DECISIONS.md ledger head **ADR-0035 → ADR-0037** (ADR-0036 split + ADR-0037 reconciliation, consecutive numbers at this commit per the parent SPEC §6.2 "if both fire at the PLAN-write commit").

### Phase-13 state-1 brainstorm

**Family pick.** `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §9 enumerates the eight feature families. At the post-12.2 close-out boundary the slate is fully open — all MVP-trunk phases 00-08 + the three HTTP-filter-family phases (09 `local_ratelimit`, 10 `rbac`, 11 `fault`) + the first Upstream-robustness-family phase (parent-12; sub-phases 12.1 + 12.2) all stand `done`. The candidates for the next phase were: (i) continue the Upstream-robustness family with `13-outlier-detection` (per-endpoint ejection on consecutive 5xx / per-host success-rate thresholds — natural family-list order after active HC) OR `13-connection-pooling` (per-protocol upstream connection pools — the named-owner phase for 06.3 REVIEW I2's residual); (ii) enter a new family (HTTP/3+QUIC, gRPC, xDS, Observability, Runtime+hot-restart, WASM-host).

**Five-dimension scoring:**

| Dimension | `13-outlier-detection` | `13-connection-pooling` | new family (HTTP/3+QUIC, gRPC, xDS, Observability, Runtime, WASM) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Carryforward closure value** | Zero (no named carryforward closes). Outlier detection is a fresh subsystem; would reuse the 12.1 `EndpointHealth` ejection seam but doesn't close anything from the standing inventory. | **HIGH.** Connection pooling is the **named-owner phase for 06.3 REVIEW I2 residual** per the 06.3 REVIEW.md §3 disposition + the 12.2 down-payment scoping. Closes BOTH (a) per-class `downstream_rq_3xx/4xx/5xx` + `cluster.<name>.upstream_rq_5xx` wire bilateral coverage AND (b) `cluster.<name>.upstream_cx_total` `value-exact` tightening. This is the single highest-value closure currently available in the standing inventory. | Zero direct closures. Some families surface their own internal carryforwards (e.g. Observability would tighten the StatsTagExtractor allow-list residual) but none close the 06.3 I2 residual. |
| **Foundation pressure (new top-level Cargo deps)** | LOW. Reuses the 12.1 `EndpointHealth` ejection seam + the 12.2 periodic-task primitive. No new crate. No ADR. | **LOW.** Reuses the 12.2 `HealthAwareHttp1Backend` harness primitive (extend in place) + the existing `ConnGaugeGuard` RAII pattern + `envoy-http1::Client` + `envoy-http2::Client`. Pool primitives live inside `envoy-http1`/`envoy-http2` (`pool.rs` modules). No new top-level Cargo dep. No new ADR projected at SPEC time (conditional ADR-0038 split LIKELY at PLAN-write; conditional ADR-0039 §6.2 revision PLAUSIBLE). | HIGH (variable). HTTP/3+QUIC needs `quinn` foundations grant; gRPC needs additional `tonic` features; xDS needs from-scratch state-machine atop `tonic` transport; Observability needs OTLP/Datadog/XRay; Runtime+hot-restart is significant new infrastructure; WASM-host is its own multi-phase sub-project. Each new family carries a foundations-grant ADR. |
| **Architectural risk** | MEDIUM. The passive-vs-active distinction is subtle (outlier detection observes data-plane responses; doesn't probe); needs careful interaction with the 12-active path. Cross-proxy timing-dependent ejection windows are hard to make deterministic for the differential harness (would need §Timing tolerances opt-in). | **MEDIUM-HIGH.** Pool primitives are the most-complex piece — H2 multiplexed-streams pool with peer-SETTINGS coordination + GOAWAY handling. But the surface is well-understood (Envoy's pool model is documented) + the per-protocol crate placement avoids cycles cleanly. The `upstream_cx_total` increment-site migration (from per-call to per-connection at pool create) is mechanical but must be atomic to avoid double-counting. The cycle-resolution decision (§5.1) is well-anticipated. | HIGH (variable). HTTP/3 introduces a new downstream listener type + a new conformance suite. gRPC complicates the H2 path. xDS introduces dynamic-config state. WASM is a full ABI + engine binding effort. |
| **Contract-surface maturity** | The `outlier_detection.*` Envoy stat tree is documented but timing-dependent. Differential observability is largely stats-based (which counter increments on which trigger) + ejection-window-bounded — harder than connection-pooling's deterministic-pool-state observable. | **HIGH.** The `cluster.<name>.upstream_cx_*` stat tree is fully documented + matures cleanly under pooling. Per-class HCM counters are already 06.3-defined and BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT-locked; phase 13 just realizes them at fixture level. The synthetic-backend pattern is 12.2-precedented. | Variable. xDS has the most mature contract (ADS state machine + effective-config diff). Observability and Runtime have moderate maturity. WASM is least-mature (ABI conformance suite still evolving upstream). |
| **First-phase scope tractability** | Tractable as a single phase if scoped to consecutive-5xx ejection only (split-gate plausible at PLAN-write but not certain). Reuses 12.x infrastructure heavily. | **MEDIUM.** ~1800-2400 LoC projected — over the §6.1 ~1500 gate. SPLIT into 13.1 + 13.2 LIKELY at PLAN-write (recommended seam: H1-only / H2-only, alternative seam: foundation-slice). Each sub-phase comes in at ~1000-1200 LoC each — manageable. | Variable. xDS family is its own multi-phase sub-project at minimum. Observability could fit as ~3 sub-phases. **Decision: `13-connection-pooling`.** Per `feedback_pick_recommendation` (always pick the recommendation; no two-option fork). The recommendation is unambiguously connection pooling because: (1) it's the **named-owner phase for the highest-value standing carryforward** (06.3 REVIEW I2 residual, deferred from 06.3 and named again at 12.2); (2) it **reuses the freshest landed harness primitive** (12.2's `HealthAwareHttp1Backend`); (3) its scope is **tractable with a known SPLIT seam** (H1-only / H2-only at sub-phase 13.1/13.2); (4) the **foundation pressure is LOW** (no new top-level Cargo dep; pool primitives are protocol-internal); (5) it **continues the Upstream-robustness family** in a natural way (active HC at 12 → pooling at 13; outlier detection + circuit breakers + retries defer to follow-up phases — all reuse the 12.x + 13.x infrastructure when they land). The decision is **NOT** "outlier detection" — outlier detection has zero carryforward closure value and timing-dependent observability that the differential harness handles less cleanly; it defers to a follow-up Upstream-robustness phase. The decision is **NOT** "enter a new family" — the project's standing posture (per `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §9 family ordering + the established Carryforward-closure-value-first heuristic from the 11/12 brainstorms) favors closing named residuals before opening new families when both are tractable.

Each sub-phase comes in at ~1000-1200 LoC — comfortably under the §6.1 gate. **Alternative seam (foundation-slice):** `13.1` = H1 + H2 pool primitives + envoy-config schema + NO new fixture (regression-equivalence via existing 19 fixtures — the 05.1 / 07.1 / 12.1 foundation-slice pattern); `13.2` = router-arm wiring + new fixture + per-class bilateral coverage + parent-13 close. **§6.2 empirical-verification findings (HEAVY; 9 items; against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`).** Performed at THIS commit by the controller directly (per the parent SPEC §6.2 + the phase-10/11/12-ratified verify-at-PLAN-write discipline). Methodology: a Docker bridge network (`p13net`) with (a) a Python-based configurable HTTP/1.1 backend container (Python 3.12-alpine; `BaseHTTPRequestHandler` with `protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"` for keep-alive support; serves 200 on `/`, 301/404/500/503 on `/301`/`/404`/`/500`/`/503`, configurable status on `/healthz` via `HEALTHZ_STATUS` env) and (b) an `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` container running an HTTP/1.1 HCM listener routing through a STRICT_DNS cluster with `circuit_breakers: { thresholds: [{ priority: DEFAULT, max_connections: 2 }] }` pointing at the backend container by container name; admin `/stats` + `/config_dump` scraped + data-plane requests driven from the host via curl + Python `http.client.HTTPConnection`. *(Initial container-name resolution attempts via `backend` failed because Docker's DNS resolves the container's full name `p13-backend`; resolved by updating the YAML.)* For item (vi) — H2 cluster stats namespace — booted a second Envoy with `typed_extension_protocol_options.envoy.extensions.upstreams.http.v3.HttpProtocolOptions.explicit_http_config.http2_protocol_options: {}` and scraped the cluster stat namespace (no H2C backend reach needed; the stat names are registered at cluster-construct time).

| # | Item | Finding | Disposition |
|---|------|---------|-------------|
| i | **`circuit_breakers.thresholds` shape + max_connections default** | `circuit_breakers: { thresholds: [{ priority?: <RoutingPriority>, max_connections?: u32, max_pending_requests?: u32, max_requests?: u32, max_retries?: u32, ... }] }`. The `priority` field defaults to `DEFAULT` (and is omitted from `/config_dump` when DEFAULT). `max_connections` default 1024 (per Envoy docs; not observed empirically because the harness load is below the cap). | **MATCHES** SPEC projection. Schema D1 lands as projected (`Cluster.circuit_breakers: Option<CircuitBreakers>` with `Thresholds` carrying `priority?: Option<RoutingPriority>` + `max_connections?: Option<u32>`; phase-13 supports DEFAULT + max_connections only; other threshold fields rejected by `deny_unknown_fields`). No ADR. |
| ii | **H1 default pool behavior under NO `circuit_breakers`** | Envoy ALWAYS pools regardless of `circuit_breakers` config (a no-`circuit_breakers` cluster + 5 requests over a single downstream keep-alive conn → `upstream_cx_total: 1`; full pool reuse). `circuit_breakers` is OPTIONAL at config-time; absence means defaults. `/config_dump` shows `circuit_breakers: "<absent>"` when not configured (Envoy doesn't echo defaults). | **MATCHES** SPEC projection. § 5.4 default-enabled-pool decision: phase-13's H1 pool runs **with hardcoded defaults when `circuit_breakers` is absent** (NOT pool-gated by the field). The 19 existing fixtures (none configures `circuit_breakers`) pool transparently. Regression-equivalence guaranteed by the existing presence-only `upstream_cx_total` assertions (no value-exact assertion to regress). No ADR. |
| iii | **H1 idle_timeout knob + default** | Knob lives at `typed_extension_protocol_options.envoy.extensions.upstreams.http.v3.HttpProtocolOptions.common_http_protocol_options.idle_timeout` (a Duration; nested deep). NOT at the cluster top-level. Default: 1 hour (3600s) per upstream Envoy docs. /config_dump shows `<absent>` for the nested field when not explicitly set. | **MATCHES** SPEC projection. §4 deferral: phase-13 (13.1 + 13.2) does NOT add the config-side `idle_timeout` knob; the pool uses a hardcoded sensible default (60s — short enough to test idle eviction in a deterministic test, long enough to not fire under fixture settle windows). The config-side knob defers to a follow-up phase. No ADR. |
| iv | **`upstream_cx_total` increment semantics + discriminating differential observable** | One increment per established upstream TCP connection. Discriminating observable shape: with a **SINGLE downstream keep-alive conn** issuing 5 sequential requests → `upstream_cx_total: 1` (full pool reuse via 1 upstream connection). With **separate downstream conns** (curl invocations) → `upstream_cx_total: N` (one upstream connect per downstream-side conn — Envoy's H1 pool returns the connection to idle AFTER the downstream conn closes, by which point the next downstream conn has already triggered a fresh upstream connect). Concurrent 4 curl jobs with `max_connections: 2` → `upstream_cx_total: 4` + `upstream_cx_overflow: 2` (max_connections is ADVISORY: Envoy increments the overflow counter but still completes the request). | **MATCHES** SPEC projection but with **CRITICAL NUANCE**. **PLAN-time fixture-shape lock-in:** fixture 0020 driver MUST issue multiple requests over a SINGLE downstream keep-alive conn to make `upstream_cx_total` the discriminating differential observable (1 vs. N). The differential harness's existing `Driver::Http1` opens one conn per request — **13.1 D10 extends the driver with `Driver::Http1KeepAlive`** (~30 LoC; mirrors 12.2's `Driver::Http1AfterSettle` precedent). NOT a wire-contract change → NO ADR fires. |
| v | **`upstream_cx_destroy` + sibling counter names + fire-sites** | Full sibling set per-cluster: `upstream_cx_destroy`, `_destroy_local`, `_destroy_remote`, `_destroy_with_active_rq`, `_destroy_local_with_active_rq`, `_destroy_remote_with_active_rq`, `upstream_cx_close_notify` (counts peer-initiated Connection: close). All fire when a pool connection is destroyed (different sub-counters for local-initiated vs remote-initiated destruction; the per-`_with_active_rq` variants fire only when destruction happens while a request was outstanding). All per-cluster (NOT per-endpoint). | **MATCHES** SPEC projection. D7 (stats): phase-13 wires the parent `upstream_cx_destroy` (always-fire sibling) + `upstream_cx_http1_total` (H1 pool connect counter) + the 13.2-landed `upstream_cx_http2_total`. The 5 sub-siblings defer to follow-up phases (no fixture deterministically forces local-vs-remote-destroy at phase-13 scope). No ADR. |
| vi | **H2 pool default behavior + max_concurrent_streams + multi-conn per endpoint** | H2 cluster stat namespace (no H2 traffic needed; Envoy registers at cluster-construct time): `cluster.<n>.upstream_cx_http1_total` (always registered; even on H2 cluster — for cross-protocol fallback), `upstream_cx_http2_total` (H2 partition), `upstream_cx_http3_total` (H3 — registered for future use). Default `max_concurrent_streams`: Envoy-as-client honors peer's `SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS` (default 100 per RFC 7540 §6.5.2 if peer doesn't send SETTINGS). Per-endpoint multi-conn threshold: Envoy spawns 2nd upstream H2 conn only when 1st is at peer's cap. Legacy cluster-field `http2_protocol_options` stays absent in `/config_dump` when `typed_extension_protocol_options` is used (Envoy's modern path). | **MATCHES** SPEC projection. 13.2 D5 H2 pool primitive design: per-endpoint connection list with `active_streams: AtomicU32` tracking + spawn 2nd conn only when 1st at peer's `SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS` cap (or cluster's `max_connections` cap, whichever is lower). 13.2 D7.2 lands the `cluster.<n>.upstream_cx_http2_total` BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT row. No ADR. |
| vii | **Per-class HCM counters under synthetic 5xx backend fixture** | Drove 6 requests through a single downstream keep-alive conn: 2× GET /(200), 1× GET /301(301), 1× GET /404(404), 1× GET /500(500), 1× GET /503(503). HCM scrape: `http.ingress_http.downstream_rq_2xx: 2`, `_3xx: 1`, `_4xx: 1`, `_5xx: 2`, `_total: 6`. Listener-namespace mirror: `listener.0.0.0.0_10000.http.ingress_http.downstream_rq_{2,3,4,5}xx` — same values. Bilateral byte-exact achievable under deterministic load. | **MATCHES** SPEC projection. 13.1 D9.1 fixture 0020 lands the per-class workload; the existing BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT rows at `:96-100` (06.3-landed `value-exact`) are EXERCISED bilaterally at the wire level for the FIRST time at this fixture — the **06.3 REVIEW I2 (a) full-closure site**. No ADR. |
| viii | **`cluster.<name>.upstream_rq_5xx` + siblings** | Same 6-request workload: cluster scrape `cluster.backend_cluster.upstream_rq_2xx: 2`, `_3xx: 1`, `_4xx: 1`, `_5xx: 2`, `_total: 6`. Cluster-namespace per-class counters match HCM-namespace per-class counters byte-exact under deterministic load (because router-proxy passes through every upstream status). | **MATCHES** SPEC projection. Fixture 0020 also asserts the cluster-namespace per-class values (a second I2 (a) closure surface). The existing BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT row at `:106` (06.3-landed `upstream_rq_5xx: value-exact`) is EXERCISED bilaterally at the wire level here for the first time. No ADR. |
| ix | **HCM filter-synth bypass on per-class counters** | **CONFIRMED.** Shut down backend → GET / → synth-503 `no healthy upstream` (body verified byte-exact = ADR-0037's 19 bytes; bonus phase-12 ADR-0037 bilateral re-confirmation). HCM `downstream_rq_5xx`: 2 → 3 (synth INCLUDED at HCM); HCM `downstream_rq_total`: 6 → 7. Cluster `upstream_rq_5xx`: 2 → 2 (synth NOT INCLUDED at cluster); Cluster `upstream_rq_total`: 6 → 6 (synth bypasses upstream → no upstream counter increment). | **MATCHES** the existing 06.3 BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT note at `:96-106` exactly ("the per-class counter is symmetric on `response_status_for_log`, agnostic to synth-vs-proxy origin" applies at HCM; cluster-level upstream_rq_* is upstream-only). Phase-13 preserves the bypass unchanged. **Bonus: ADR-0037's 19-byte `no healthy upstream` body bilaterally re-confirmed in passing** (a useful re-validation of the 12.2 implementation). No ADR. |

**§6.2 synthesis: ALL 9 items MATCHED the parent-13 SPEC's projections.** No empirical-revision ADR fires at the state-2 split commit. **Cycle-resolution decision (PLAN lock-in #1) — picked per `feedback_pick_recommendation`:** the 13.1 SPEC §5.1 left the seam open between (a) a new trait declared in `envoy-cluster` (`H1ClientPool` trait implemented by `envoy-http1::H1Pool`; held as `Cluster.h1_pool: Option<Arc<dyn H1ClientPool>>`) vs (b) bin-wired injection via an external `H1PoolManager` registry sibling-to-`ClusterManager`. PLAN-time PICK: option (b). Rationale: (1) option (a) requires interior mutability on `Cluster` (the `Arc<Cluster>` from `from_bootstrap` has no setter), OR widening `from_bootstrap`'s signature to take a `pool_builder` callback, OR chicken-and-egg pre-building with `Cluster.cx_total` registration — all intrusive. (2) option (b) parallels the 12.2 `envoy-health::Scheduler` precedent verbatim — `envoy-bin` builds `cluster_mgr` first via `from_bootstrap`, then `H1PoolManager::for_bootstrap` second (walks bootstrap clusters; looks up each in `cluster_mgr` to grab shared `Arc<Counter>`/`Arc<Gauge>` stat handles; builds one `H1Pool` per H1 cluster); the HCM proxy arm gets the pool manager plumbed alongside `cluster_mgr` at HCM-config construction. (3) NO new trait in `envoy-cluster`; only `ConnGaugeGuard` gains a public `from_gauge` constructor (4-line addition) so pools can construct guards against the shared cluster gauge handle. (4) NO new top-level Cargo dep (per lock-in #9). (5) NO ADR fires (per lock-in #16). If state-3 execution surfaces a non-obvious lifecycle complication (e.g. the HCM-config-construction site has poor ergonomic reach to `Arc<H1PoolManager>`), the controller documents the surfacing finding in PROGRESS + lands an inline ADR resolving it (NOT projected).

Pre-fix, `H2PoolGuard::Drop` ran `active_streams.fetch_sub(1)` OUTSIDE the `connections.lock()`, opening a window where a concurrent Phase-1 walker in `acquire()` could CAS-claim the stream slot on the to-be-evicted entry, leading to orphaned PoolGuards with broken `established` accounting and falsely-fired `cx_destroy`. Post-fix the invalidate branch takes `connections.lock()` BEFORE the fetch_sub and holds it across both the decrement and the `retain()`. The non-invalidate branch keeps the original lock-free fetch_sub (residual race benign by the sweeper's `active_streams != 0` early-return invariant; documented in a correctness-argument comment block). Also added an H1 race-regression stress test `pool_acquire_after_concurrent_release_1000_iterations_zero_spurious_overflows` (probabilistic 1000-iter exercise of the pre-fix race window; post-fix produces 0 spurious overflows; runs in ~90ms). 3 files touched (+144 / -16 LoC net).
